newsitem.title: USA: Schnitzer sees improved scrap metal prices.
newsitem.headline: Schnitzer sees improved scrap metal prices.

text.p: Schnitzer Steel Industries Inc. Monday said scap metal prices improved in the third quarter ended in May and the company expects further improvement in the current quarter.

"Market conditions for both buying and selling ferrous scrap have improved since the second quarter and, as a result, the company's operating margin has increased significantly," the company said in a statement accompanying its third quarter results. "Our average selling price for ferrous scrap rose from $131 per ton in the second quarter to $140 per ton this quarter. Our aggressive management of prices at the scale while selling prices were falling earlier this year also reduced our cost per ton significantly this quarter. Based on bookings so far for the fourth quarter, we expect to see even further improvement in prices during that period."

Earlier Schnitzer reported net income of $8.4 million or $0.81 a share on revenues of $89.3 million for the three months ended May 31, 1997. That compares with net income of $4.6 million or $0.44 per share on revenues of $87.0 million a year ago. The latest quarter included a gain of approximately $3 million, or $0.19 a share, upon settlement of an interest rate agreement.
